prompt: Prime-time adult animated sitcom characters with simple rounded cartoon bodies, flat colour and black outlines, but every face is painted with startling real skin: pores, stubble, wrinkles, wet tired eyes, real eyelids, far more lifelike than anything around it, no feature exaggerated. Every colour is laid on in thick visible oil brushstrokes. Close, waist up, inside a secret 1930s basement speakeasy: three people dancing arm in arm in a high-kicking line, laughing: on the left, a short stout white man in his sixties with ginger mutton-chop whiskers, a red tie and a red carnation in his lapel; in the middle, a tall skinny mayor in a bowler hat with a heavy gold mayoral chain round his neck, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks and a pencil-thin grey moustache; on the right, a broad-shouldered white woman in her fifties with a black bob, a long nose, a plain blue cardigan and a blue carnation, real-skinned faces large in frame, eyes creased with laughter, a gold spotlight full on them. Dust and grit shake down from the wooden ceiling above in fine streams with every stamp of the boots on the street overhead, catching the light. Behind them, soft, emerald lamps, scarlet velvet and blank green paper money with no printing drifting in the air. Most of the frame warm shadow; the brightest values are the spotlight on their faces and the falling dust. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
